title: Beyond the 956: Arnaldo Coen, leading Mexican artist of the Generación de la Ruptura, dies at 86
excerpt: Arnaldo Coen, the Mexican painter, sculptor and muralist who helped lead the Generación de la Ruptura, has died at 86. His wife, gallerist Lourdes Sosa, announced his death on Sunday, November 8, 2026.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Arnaldo Coen, the Mexican painter, sculptor and muralist who helped lead the Generación de la Ruptura, has died at 86.

Coen died on Sunday, November 8, 2026, in Mexico City. His wife, gallerist Lourdes Sosa, announced his death in a message remembering his creativity, curiosity and passion for life. The Instituto Nacional de Bellas Artes y Literatura (INBAL) also confirmed his death and expressed its condolences. No cause of death has been released.

Born June 10, 1940, in Mexico City, Coen became one of the leading figures of the Generación de la Ruptura, the movement that broke with the traditions of Mexican muralism and opened new paths for contemporary art in Mexico. In 1968 he was a founder of the Salón Independiente, and his work over more than six decades ranged across painting, sculpture, object art, environments and body art, as well as scenography and costume design for theatre and dance, exploring the links between painting, space, geometry and music.

His works were shown at the Palacio de Bellas Artes and the Museo de Arte Moderno, and are held in museum collections in Mexico and abroad, including the Museo Universitario Arte Contemporáneo (MUAC) at UNAM. He received the Premio Nacional de Ciencias y Artes in 2014 and the Medalla Bellas Artes in Visual Arts in 2022, and was a member of the Academia de Artes.

Sources: El Universal; El Heraldo de México; Instituto Nacional de Bellas Artes y Literatura (INBAL); Ahora Noticias.
